title: Design: Claude trading desk: a desk-manager session over specialist lanes (market watch, entry review, in-trade management = LTR, exit/post-trade grading), decisions as package-level intents through per-account risk, sandbox/paper first, every decision a point-in-time record the models train on
note: [2026-10-25 16:14Z session_01UKBXozpiJicMHHyMp47MnN] Operator 16:12Z asked whether to scope a 'trading desk manager': lanes for entries, market monitoring, adjustments and exits, managed by one desk session, in a sandbox, with all decisions recorded so the system and models can execute on them. Manager view: yes, scope it as a design after the LTR prototype has run on real trades for a few days, so the design starts from measured review rows (cost/decision, latency, hit rate). Dispatch after LTR-4 is live. [2026-10-25 ~16:20-16:22Z session_01UKBXozpiJicMHHyMp47MnN] OPERATOR INPUTS (chat, close paraphrase): (1) the desk RELIES ON THE REPO for context: the repo produces specific outputs (a per-decision 'decision packet') so Claude is applied only to the important judgment and context, not to building context or redoing research each time; this keeps a consistent pattern and makes outputs fit the datasets the models train on and the live trade management uses. (2) Balance usage vs learning: do not waste usage on routine decisions, but do use powerful models where we learn: 'at least some of them should be Opus, or maybe it's enough if Opus is doing the review and not the actual live management'. (3) Make sure the lanes have what they need to perform live management. (4) Timeframe: see how small we can get; '15 minutes is feasible in any case', and drive it lower. MANAGER PROPOSAL to carry into the design: L0 deterministic packet + due-watch (no model); L1 Haiku gate; L2 Sonnet live decisions on the packet; L3 Opus on escalations PLUS a sampled share of decisions re-judged blind by Opus as teacher labels for distillation, and the weekly grading. Measure end-to-end latency (bar close -> decision recorded) in the LTR prototype as the baseline for the 15m target. [2026-10-25 ~16:27Z session_01UKBXozpiJicMHHyMp47MnN] OPERATOR (chat, close paraphrase): (5) scope a lane that STAYS LIVE for short-timeframe trades (10 min to 1 h holds): what would it cost, could it be profitable, which timeframes are feasible, and can we build a flow that works. (6) Decision packets are the SAME data feed for Claude and the ML models: Claude infers a decision from the packet, the ML models learn from Claude's inference (Claude decisions = training data), and when ML does live trade management, Claude's recommendations are included in that pipeline (as an input). DESIGN MUST ANSWER for (5): measured cost/decision and latency from the LTR prototype; standing-lane cost per hour at 1m/5m/15m cadence incl. context growth and rotation; edge net of full cost at those horizons from existing scalp harnesses (ict_scalp, chop_scalp, fvg_range) or new Stage-0 units; break-even = usage cost per trade vs expected R x risk. For (6): one packet schema shared by Claude and ML; Claude label vs realized outcome both kept (Claude is a teacher, never ground truth); Claude-as-feature only where Claude is available at inference time (CJ design Q2 'Allow as a feature later'); point-in-time info_cutoff on every row. [2026-10-25 17:36Z session_01UKBXozpiJicMHHyMp47MnN] Operator ~17:35Z: push the desk design faster; prioritize it above other builds (not replace, may supersede some). Dispatched NOW (Opus $14) instead of after LTR-4 data; design uses first-run measurements (LTR-3 run, packet build ~36 s) and marks the rest unmeasured. Reshapes: CJ-2 now waits on it (dataset schema = desk packet schema); LTR-6/8/9 re-scoped by its intent->per-account-risk path; LTR-5 grading folds into its grading section.
